increase.label: increase and flourishing
increase.reading: Seek an increase in the valued result: livelihood, customers, achievement, creative work, or another desired good.
increase.boundary: Translate increase by analogy; do not claim that fertility texts originally concerned trade, school, or media.

petition.label: petition for a favorable response
petition.reading: Seek a favorable response from an agent whose cooperation matters, including a creator, teacher, customer, or institution.
petition.boundary: A modern person is not identified with a deity. The ritual petitioner asks divine aid concerning the desired response.

provision.label: provision and reciprocal giving
provision.reading: Provide something valued and seek a favorable reception, including a successful shop, service, offering, or shared meal.
provision.boundary: Preserve the source recipient; food in an offering does not make a deity a patron of a modern food business.

renewal.label: cleansing and a fresh beginning
renewal.reading: Seek a fresh beginning or restoration of a person’s condition before a new undertaking.
renewal.boundary: The modern obstacle is an analogy, not evidence of historical impurity.

release.label: removal of an unwanted condition
release.reading: Seek to remove illness, trouble, obstruction, anxiety, or another unwanted condition.
release.boundary: Do not invent a hostile person or enemy for an ordinary difficulty.

protection.label: protection from harm
protection.reading: Seek protection for a person or community from a feared loss or harmful influence.
protection.boundary: Do not interpret competition alone as a demand to harm a rival.

persistence.label: waiting through a transition
persistence.reading: Seek change that requires sustained waiting or a passage through time, including completion of a new work.
persistence.boundary: An overnight rite is a temporal analogy, not an attested practice for productivity.

general.label: a petition for the desired outcome
general.reading: Express a wish whose modern circumstances have no close counterpart in this small corpus. Use the general structure of giving and petition without inventing an ancient specialty.
general.boundary: This is a broad reconstruction; no specific ancient purpose is claimed.

passage.label: passage into a different place or condition
passage.reading: Cross a boundary, enter unfamiliar surroundings, gain access, or move into a new phase. Physical passage can serve as an explicit modern analogy for these changes.
passage.boundary: The original passage may belong to purification. Do not claim it was historically used for modern travel or admission; preserve that distinction without forbidding the analogy.
